This game is exactly my thing. But it makes some fatal UX mistakes that the dev insists on not fixing. Let me explain: To play this game, you'll be clicking a LOT. There are hundreds of character classes, dozens of monsters, dozens of symbols you've never seen before. Your characters will be changing class multiple times throughout the game, earning new dice with new symbols on every run. So, you'll need to be clicking dice and reading the pop-up descriptions a lot. OK. I accept this! I see no way around it! That's fine! Here's the problem: When you roll dice, they're scattered all over the place. This die is upside down. This other die is sideways. Your top guy's die is second from the bottom. Your second guy's die is third. Your third guy's die is at the top. Your fourth guy's die is kind of next to your first guy's die. And where's your fifth guy's die? Oh, it's over there. Ok, I've decided which dice I'm keeping and which dice I'm re-rolling. Click re-roll... and there they go again. Scattered all over the place. Wouldn't it be nice if they all lined up automatically after you rolled them, so you could see at a glance which die corresponded with which character? After all, the dev has thrown you into this chaotic jungle of never-before-seen symbols and terms. You could play for 500 hours and you won't have memorized all the meanings, effects, and interactions. You'll have to click... click... click to read about them, many times each turn. That depth and complexity is what you buy into when you play this game. I'm willing to do it. I'm happy to do it, in fact, if you're willing to meet me halfway. But could ya throw me a bone here? It's the most obvious QoL feature -- put rolled dice where it's obvious what character they belong to. It's such an obvious QoL feature that, surprise, it's actually in the game already... but you have to double-click to do it. On each and every die roll. After you already clicked once to roll the dice. There's no global setting. I'm already clicking constantly. Why won't you let me toggle on an "auto-line-up" option? I'm clicking 3 times for every die roll when I only need to click once. Actually, make that 4 times. Because, for some reason, when you click "re-roll" after you've lined the dice up, they don't re-roll. Instead, they scatter around. You have to click re-roll AGAIN to get them to re-roll. Everything else in this game is so well-thought-out, it makes it really grating that the dev forces you to click 4 times on each roll just to get the dice to line up neatly. I'm out unless that gets fixed.

Good dice game. Had a successful first run rolling dice, taking risks, upgrading. Now for my third run I was screen sharing with my brother to show him what it's was about and we ended up strategizing our way to the final fight. But as it turns out my build had a wizard boost all my healers pips by 1, lost the wizard, lost my damage dealer, had a paladin who's dice got perma petrified. My healer could only increase max HP and Regen till the boss kept summoning demons who kept summoning imps. Mathematically they couldn't do more than 30 DMG at one time if they focuses one character. I had like 32 Regen and 60+ HP on my 3 remaining characters. One of which was the before mentioned paladin with all his dice turned to stone. A healer who could only increase max HP or heal/mana +4 to cast Regen or a 2 magic damage spell. And one sharpshooter with only a 6hp or less insta kill die face and a 3 DMG ranged attacks. All of which after killing the boss left me with 100 reinforcements of demons that were summoned that had been summoning imps while I struggled. And after about an extra hour of killing demons slowly finding imps here and there in the horde of demons. The game said somethings along the lines of "too many commands: YOU LOSE" As the game promptly crashed....... If any of that made sense to you all I can say is: If the game itself gave up, on itself, I think i won.

This game is okay. The main mode is well balanced and interesting, but the game is essentially a sequence of random battles. There is no pathing, and your team composition can't really be built around any foreknowledge other than the breadth of possible upcoming fights. Where this game really struggles is in its feature bloat. There are dozens of keywords, and many lack clear descriptions. This makes them difficult to parse, which detracts from the game considering how many there are. The complexity-to-depth ratio is off kilter, and it seems like the game would be more interesting if it were simplified somewhat. But perhaps the worst thing about the game is its handling of difficulty. The core gameplay is really well balanced, and higher difficulties provide an interesting challenge. Unfortunately, at very high difficulties, it is possible to lose in the first combat. No big deal, just try again... right? Well, no, actually. You will have to go play another mode because you didn't make it far enough to start a fresh run. This means that high difficulty modes are not only difficult, but also require that you waste your time if you encounter an impossible start. I would have enjoyed climbing the difficulties of this game like in Slay the Spire or Monster Train, but this insistence on wasting the player's time at higher difficulties has turned me off the game. I (came back to edit this review, and) don't think I've touched the game in over a year.

I think this game falls short of other games in the genre, like Circadian Dice (which is cheaper and a genuine masterpiece of game design.) The game moves at a sluggish pace, and doubles down on the RNG by not having any smoothing devices (no one-off items, etc) and by not giving the player any build control (no shops, etc). Essentially, it's like a restrained puzzle game where sometimes you just lose. Finally, it's aimless: the challenges aren't sequential, there's no "campaign" -- it's just a system they lay out through challenges, which is thoroughly done but not very enticing. So to me it feels like the worst of both worlds. It's not a great puzzle game, and it's not a great party RPG game. It's not even a particularly interesting dice game. The end result is something that's polished but just not that fun. It is effective at taking up your time, though.

In general, I like the game, the gameplay system, graphics, music, gameplay modes, other niceties, however, I do not recommend it because of the poorly balanced difficulty levels. Easy level is medium+, medium level is hard, etc. If you make a game and add an easy level then make it f****n easy! I played on easy level and I get frustrated because the enemies already have very strong attacks and my fighters are still misers with little attacks. A played many fights before. Also, how is it possible that the Bosses are divided into smaller units that collectively have more energy after the division than the Boss himself ? Where is the logic here ? A dying boss produces super strong units ? Or the dice keep drawing X when I have 5 divided strong opponents, and I was at 19th fight - with such a round on easy you should be supporting the player and you are supporting the SI. Something is definitely wrong there.... So eventely this game is waste of my time. And this is the most unpleasant thing.

I hate to leave a negative review for this because I actually liked the game for the dozen hours I played it, but the lack of content is definitely too severe to get a pass. I expected more and more enemies, bosses and items; in reality, there's very few, and the entire gimmick is to unlock bizarre game-modes with strange rules and modifiers, which I have zero interest in. All I wanted is a true endless mode that extended for much longer, instead, the so-called endless mode just loops the same run over and over resetting the entire party on every iteration.

In its current state for Steam, I cannot recommend this game. I enjoy it immensely, but the constant crashing is not just disruptive, but sometimes can softlock the run, requiring you to quit. I will happily change my review when this bug is fixed.

I wanted to love this but couldn't get into it. I have hundreds of hours in Slay the Spire and was hoping for something similar that could capture the thrill of manipulating your state to a place where you feel overpowered or just powered enough to win. Slice & Dice though, is a game about getting out of jam. Always. Every turn is a puzzle to get out of a jam - the jam being one of more of your party dying. In StS death comes quickly, it's fairly obvious you're not going to make it. In Slice & Dice death comes every turn and your job is to prevent it. Slowly. It feels like wading through treacle. The whole re-roll and undo mechanic makes it very clear that this is a puzzle game. Not my cup of tea. Appreciate the craft that has gone into it and I also appreciate this is a brilliant cup of tea for others.

I've played many, many other games of this variety, most notably Astrea which is also a dice-builder. Unfortunately, like Astrea, this one just doesn't capture my long term interest. I can't point to anything in particular being "wrong" with the game, although the balance feels biased more toward making do with the hand you were dealt, rather than progressively working on developing your party. Maybe it's the feeling of progression that I am missing? After 5 hours I've beaten the game with a couple different party compositions and don't feel any particular draw to play it again and grind the harder modes. Point being that even if you've poured countless hours into games such as Slay the Spire, Balatro, etc... even with all the positive reviews it's not a guarantee this game will scratch the same itch for you. Play the demo first to see if sets a hook.

Slice & Dice 骰子与砍杀：S+ 想法简单设计精妙数值优雅，但底层设计决定偶尔吃屎体验的骰子肉鸽极佳作 （第一段仅与成就有关，如果不在意这方面请自行跳过）首先，我想要劝退所有成就党，请不要！请不要！请不要尝试开坑这个游戏！太多的成就太考验RNG，甚至有一系列的chaos+成就到现在我都没想到什么理论上能够成立的解决方法，就算是有理论上解法的部分成就，也相当相当依赖RNG，并且碰瓷（是的，就是碰瓷，因为某些成就要求的概率实在是过于过于的夸张了）RNG的过程也相当无聊，更不要说有hell win-streak这种逆天难度模式的连胜，目前排行榜能完成的人也仅为个位数（并且我认为其中有人一定使用了作弊手段或者MOD），还有100000死亡这种累计数据的成就（考虑到难度来说，这个还算是相当简单），如果你是一个非常在意成就完成度的人，恳请你绕路以防像我这样刷了半天个别成就暗暗破防 接下来我就要大夸特夸了！ 1. 简洁的骰面机制，近乎完美的执行：这款游戏从概念来说，不是很新颖，每个英雄一个骰子，每一个骰面对应一些能力，通过能力来进行各种操作从而战胜敌人，甚至可以说有点俗套，但是这款游戏在骰子这方面的设计真的是拉满了，不同英雄具有不同的骰面并且适合不同的阵容和道具，如果我没有记错的话从一级到三级分为五种大类型总共有一百八十个左右的英雄，基本上每个英雄我光是看画像就能够知道每个骰面是什么了，记忆点非常强。黄色的英雄一般是战士，具有中上的输出，并且多带有一定的防御能力血量也偏高；橙色英雄一般有高输出，并且具有独特的攻击方面的能力，例如cantrip可以提供投掷时的伤害，poison能够提供打boss时的长线输出，ranged能够提供远程敌人的解决手段等等；灰色英雄一般起到防御的作用，能够为队友提供护甲，保证队伍脆皮不会轻易被带走；蓝色英雄鞥能够提供法力并且根据英雄获得对应的法术，通过消耗法术来施法；红色英雄一般能够提供治疗与少量法力，保证队伍在防不下来的攻击前能够保持较好的血量状态，并且是游戏比较直接的cleanse来源，用于消除负面状态；还有自身比较特殊的绿色，每个英雄基本都带有不同的特殊能力。其实光是五个阵营的搭配就有很多可以说的，更不要说每一个英雄自己骰面的设计，比如灰色的英雄即使在防御方面也有对应擅长的领域，比如valkyrie能够提供少有的复活，但是自己在队友阵亡前能够做出的贡献相对于其他的角色较低，很多时候能够盘活励志局但在比较顺的局反而可能拖后腿，stalwart能够提供灰色里面少有的cleanse但是没有装备的加持很多时候能给予的防御有限，poet能够联动法师提供一定的法力，防御与法力挂钩，但是自己的法术较为拉垮，且在第一回合法师出现较差的骰面时用处不如其他的灰色。这里就不一一赘述了，总之，骰面的设计非常优秀，每个英雄都很有记忆点（虽然还是有个别感觉略凑数的） 2. 美如画的词条。这个游戏有接近300个词条，虽然看上去多，但是很多（接近两百多个）词条都是作为个别装备的类似于彩蛋存在的，实际上经常用的可能就几十个，而且一般来说都不难理解，很多的词条设计的真的特别有风味，比如deathwish遗愿能够让你的英雄处于濒死状态的时候数值翻倍，完美贴合自己将要临终时回光返照、殊死一搏的感觉，并且通过击杀敌人从而脱离濒死状态会导致遗愿失效，非常有设计感美感；inspired激励当你的上一个骰面数字更高时会让数值翻倍，比如说3inspired需要4点及以上的骰面来翻倍，而当时3inspired被触发变成6之后，就能够去inspire5点的inspired骰面，就好像在战场上需要有一个人先来鼓舞士气，从而让后续的士兵能够一个接一个地把这个士气传递下去，画面感很强的词条。唉，实在是太多太好的词条可以拿出来说了，设计水平真的非常高！这里就不再展开了 3. 性感的装备。游戏通过进行的层数每个阶段给予对应等级的装备，当然也有其他的方式（比如challenge blessing）来提供少量的额外装备，这个游戏除去几乎纯彩蛋的0级装备应该是有三百加的装备，每个装备（呃可能是大部分略有几个装备感觉凑数的）都独特具有自己的作用，比如说2级（忘记名字了毕竟是英文的有点没记住）能够替换上下两个面为pain cantrip加一次投掷的装备，相当于单纯给一提供三分之一的重掷效果，但是提供较大的血量压力，但是拿到了四级中消除红色词条的道具，就能够实现无损加重掷，并且与其他的cantrip效果配合能够在正式进行操作之前造成很高的伤害，甚至可以直接无限。这个游戏让人感觉有点无从说起的地方就是他的内容实在是太多太满了，真的有点感觉无从说起，装备如果细讲也能够说很久...限于篇幅就先说这些 4. 照样美如画、差异化拉满的怪物设计。很多这种策略肉鸽游戏陷入了己方设计拉满，而对策的敌人则拉垮，仅为数值提升的站桩木棍的局面，这个游戏的70多个（好像刚好就是七十个？）怪物，可以说每一个都有独特的骰面，以及擅长的内容以及缺点。比如说就是最简单的蜜蜂和老鼠，同样都是造成较低的伤害，但是蜜蜂有最左边的骰面能够自杀造成5点伤害，如果在第一回合就摇出来威胁性远超老鼠，但是其自身血量低老鼠一点，更容易被解决从而减少巨量威胁；墓碑虽然只有三滴血，但是每一滴血都需要单独移除，也就是要求三次伤害，如果你的队伍伤害非常高，但是段数非常低，就会比较折磨，但是其召唤出来的骷髅自带亡语能够对上下的敌人造成一点伤害，导致在解决墓碑的召唤物时同时也会解决墓碑，而且墓碑自己每次都只会收到一点伤害，骷髅的亡语完美契合，可以说非常自洽优雅的设计思路，太多太多优秀的怪物可以说了，鉴于已经写了太长了就先这样…（感觉真的特别不好意思，因为这个游戏实在是有太多好的方面需要好好品鉴评价:-）） 5. 繁多个性化的游戏模式。光是我能够想到的classic heaven, easy, hard, unfair, brutal, hell，还有更多的loot, shortcut, choose-party, nightmare, fight, raid等，creative里面的wish, paste，curse里面的各种诅咒模式，crappy里面一些彩蛋性质的模式，实在是太多太多，能够看出来制作者真的特别喜欢他设计的游戏！（我也是！） 6. 重复性极低的进阶系统。这个游戏的进阶是通过设计点数，需要选择不同难度的诅咒来达成对应的点数条件来提高难度的，具体的我下面结合缺点说 7. 相当对味的像素风。 接下来我就要吐槽一些缺点了:( 1. 游戏的高难度曲线非常不平滑，首先要声明，从easy到hard的曲线还是非常平滑的，整体感受还是不错的，但是从hard到unfair到brutal再到hell，尤其是后两个就相当陡峭了，其实后两个我觉得除非是单纯挑战，基本上没有游玩的必要（），从unfair开始给予的10个诅咒点数就能够有很大的压力，并且由于进阶系统是让你自己选择，而且每次选择都是从挑选的几个中再挑几个，导致很多时候有些过于变态的诅咒其实根本不会选，比如big 游戏因为是扔骰子，而每次通常只会有两次重掷的机会，就导致有时候运气非常差会直接崩盘，比如说你的阵容mountain以两位法师为核心，在最后的boss战时boss和小怪直接攻击法师，而这个时候你的灰色英雄刚好roll了三次全是比较无关痛痒的防御或者直接roll到了空白或者直接roll到了攻击骰面同时又秒不掉小怪，你的蓝色英雄很有可能直接因此被抬走直接崩盘，或者你这局游戏完全没看到cleanse词条，但是在最后一关巨龙直接一上来一口毒吐上去，你输出又不够紧凑能够两三回合内解决，如果巨龙一上来aoe或者咬你可能就赢了，这就是糟心的点，有时候不同阵容给予的不同的boss的不同意图方差过大，有时候你感觉你已经尽力在防了，但是就是因为RNG所以输了，会感觉非常的懊恼，像是杀戮尖塔偶尔也会鬼抽，但是因为有换牌药等能够提供一定的容错，而这个游戏你运气差的时候真的可以在毫无防备的情况下被送走，我有一次两个法师在最后一局打hexia的对局中，连续两回合三次投掷一次法力面都没有，而法力面刚好概率都是二分之一，也就两个是二分之一的六次方相乘，我也是佩服… Party-building roguelike, with turn-based combat. Each of your 5 heroes has a different class, and each class (and enemy type) has a die to determine which of 6 possible actions they can take that turn. At the end of each fight, you receive either a class promotion or a held item for one of your heroes. The meat of the game comes from the enormous number of classes. These are divided into 6 archetypes that map fairly nicely onto classic rpg archetypes (tank, dps, healer, etc.), and then further split into 3 tiers- heroes start in a tier 1 class, and can promote to tier 3 by the end of the run. Heroes must promote into a new class 1 tier up, from the same archetype, and you get 2 random promotions to choose between. This results in your build constantly evolving, as you can't just have your heroes grow into "the same, with bigger numbers". Enemy variety is almost as great as hero variety, and every possible tactic has a certain enemy that counters it. The enemies in the next battle are revealed before you choose your reward from the previous one, so the choice you make often features tension between synergy with your overall party, and specific effectiveness against the next enemy. This describes the Classic mode, but the game features a huge number (20+) of alternative modes, from challenges to sandboxes. If any part of the Classic gameplay loop frustrates or annoys you, there is likely an alternate mode that reworks or removes it. Metaprogression comes through achievement based unlocks for most classes, items, and modes, to avoid overwhelming a new player with all the complexity at once. Don't want that restriction? No worries- there's an Unlock All option available from the very start, which still lets you track achievements. And this what stands out most about Slice & Dice- its commitment to letting you play the way you want. This is the real secret to its high review score, and more developers should take note!
